title: Fix the no-posted-transactions report
prompt: This function should return the accounts that have no posted transaction, but it always comes back empty. Find the bug and fix `solve(accounts, transactions)`.
rules: Only transactions whose `status` is `posted` count. An account whose transactions are all pending or declined has no posted transaction.
Include accounts of every status: active, closed and frozen.
Return every column of `accounts`, in the same order, with the same types.
hints: Both tables have a column called `status`. After the join, which table's `status` is the filter looking at?
A left anti join returns only the columns of the left table, so the filter tests the account's status, which is never `posted`.
Filter `transactions` to posted ones first, then anti join `accounts` against that smaller table.
explanation: The filter is on the wrong side. A left anti join returns only the columns of `accounts`, so `F.col("status") == "posted"` after the join tests the account's status (active, closed or frozen), which is never `posted`, and every row drops. The status we care about belongs to the transactions, so filter them before the join: `posted = transactions.filter(F.col("status") == "posted")`, then `accounts.join(posted, on="account_id", how="left_anti")`. Simply deleting the filter isn't enough: an account whose only transaction was declined would then be left out.
